expectations.text: Report covers all six dimensions: API Contract, Error Envelope, Exception Handling, Project Structure, System Design Decisions, and Prisma Error Mapping
expectations.evidence: Report has clearly labeled sections for all six dimensions

expectations.text: Report catches the error envelope violation: api-response.ts uses { success: false, error } but contract requires { error } with no success field
expectations.evidence: Explicitly cited utils/api-response.ts:13-17 and app.ts error handler branches

expectations.text: Report catches the health route try-catch violation: health.ts has a try-catch around a DB call, which violates the zero try-catch rule for route handlers
expectations.evidence: Cited routes/health.ts:7-13 as a violation of Layer 3 rule

expectations.text: Report catches the TTL defaulting violation: url.ts always sets expiresAt even when no ttlDays is provided, but spec requires expiresAt: null in that case
expectations.evidence: Cited routes/url.ts:48-54, noted expiresAt uses DEFAULT_URL_TTL_DAYS fallback instead of null

expectations.text: Report uses checkmark/cross/warning markers to distinguish compliant, violated, and missing items
expectations.evidence: Report uses Compliant/Violations/Not Yet Implemented headers with appropriate content

expectations.text: Priority Fix List contains only violations, not missing features
expectations.evidence: Priority Fix List items 1-7 all reference actual code violations, not unimplemented features

expectations.text: At least one violation cites a specific file:line reference
expectations.evidence: Multiple file:line references throughout, e.g. routes/url.ts:154, utils/api-response.ts:6-10
